messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @maria.s (primary oncall) — detected repeated NotReady flaps for nodes in inference-prod-pool across us-west-2. 3 nodes NotReady in 6m, kubelet restarts observed. Severity: P1.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1143. Initial metric spikes: increased 5xxs to hosted-api routes backed by inference-prod.
maria.s: ack — digging in. which instances? any pattern on instance type?
sre-runner: I see node names: ip-10-0-72-21, ip-10-0-80-33, ip-10-0-65-10. All g5.2xlarge, same kernel version. kubelet logs show repeated segfaults in nvidia-device-plugin and kubelet restart.
kevin: I can run a quick healthcheck and cordon the most affected node to stop scheduling new pods.
maria.s: please do. Also ramp down traffic to inference-prod for critical customers while we triage — thundering herd risk. @aubrey can you open a customer-impact thread?
aubrey: on it. posting to #customer-success and pinging key CS contacts for customers with VIP routing.
kevin: cordon ip-10-0-80-33 now:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-80-33
kubectl drain ip-10-0-80-33 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
kevin: drain completed, pods rescheduled to other nodes. noticing one inference container crashloop on restart (OOM on startup).
maria.s: which model endpoint?
kevin: model: gpt-small-v2, container logs show CUDA out-of-memory on warmup. Possibly simultaneous restarts + no GPU reclaim.
tim_r: I’m scaling the deployment replicas down temporarily and enabling model fallback to cpu-hosted variant for non-latency-critical traffic.
sre-runner: also increasing node auto-replace: set autoscaler to add 2 nodes to pool.
jackie: tagging infra to do a rolling restart of the device plugin daemonset after node stabilization — might be stale driver state causing kubelet crashes.
aubrey: CS update: A handful of enterprise customers saw 5xx spikes for ~4–12s per request, error rate peaked at 2.4% for inference endpoints. We notified customers A and C and offered failover guidance.
maria.s: timeline so far: 12:04 oncall-bot alerts -> 12:05 cordon/drain node -> 12:08 OOM discovered -> 12:10 scale + fallback engaged -> 12:18 autoscaler adding nodes -> 12:24 device plugin rolling restart begun.
kevin: running remote systemctl on the node to try kubelet restart after crash loop: `ssh ec2-user@ip-10-0-65-10 "sudo systemctl restart kubelet"`
kevin: kubelet came back to Ready on ip-10-0-65-10 at ~12:26 but then flapped again once after a GPU driver rebind attempt.
maria.s: is there evidence of GPU driver crashes? paste relevant snippet.
sre-runner: logs:
```
/nvidia-driver/error: nvidia_uvm: Fatal: GPU page fault at 0x7ff.. iommu error
kubelet: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
... stacktrace ...
"SIGSEGV" in nvidia-container-runtime
```
kevin: I’m removing pods with high init concurrency and applying a startup probe to serialise warmups. Patch applied to inference deployments: reduce parallelism to 1 for warmup.
aubrey: customer-success: we advised customers to switch to region fallback (us-east-1) and offered mitigation tokens. A and C accepted reroute. D requested SLA credit; we'll escalate to Billing later.
jackie: device-plugin rollout finished at 12:36. nodes report healthy device plugin + GPU counts. Tests show one failing kernel driver on ip-10-0-72-21 — planning targeted AMI replace for that host.
maria.s: mitigation checklist executed: cordon/drain, restart kubelet, device-plugin restart, replicas throttled, model fallback enabled, autoscaler increased. Current status: 2 nodes still flapped earlier but stable now. Error rate down to 0.2%. Latency back to baseline for most traffic.
kevin: one lingering issue: a single pod still OOMs on restart — we’ve left it on fallback cpu variant. Will collect heap/profile.
tim_r: opening a follow-up task to add startup memory limits and better OOM-out handling in runtime: TASK-OPS-2201.
sre-runner: recording CRITICAL observability gaps: missing per-pod gpu-memory telemetry at warmup; will add exporter.
aubrey: CS summary sent at 12:48 to customers: short blip, most traffic auto-routed, mitigation in place, engineering postmortem to follow.
maria.s: I'm going to prepare a handoff to night oncall @kevin (taking over) — current state: cluster stabilized, one node flagged for AMI replace, one pod on cpu-fallback. Please keep monitoring for 2h.
kevin: ack takeover. I'll monitor nodes and watch for kubelet restarts. If flapping resumes, plan is to cordon and force-terminate problematic instance and trigger replacement.
maria.s: notes for handoff (copy into #inc-1789998888):
- root cause: suspected GPU driver/kernel fault causing nvidia device plugin segfault and kubelet panics leading to NotReady flaps.
- mitigations performed: cordon/drain x2 nodes, kubelet restarts, device-plugin rolling restart, reduced warmup concurrency, enabled cpu fallback, scaled autoscaler +2.
- customer impact: small % of 5xxs for ~15m window, targeted customers notified.
- next steps: AMI replace for ip-10-0-72-21, add GPU warmup memory metrics, harden startup OOM handling, postmortem and RCA.
kevin: taking notes. Will send a brief status ping at +30m and +90m.
jackie: filing postmortem draft and attaching logs: PM-INC-1789998888-draft.
aubrey: thanks all — nice quick coordination. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Handoff completed: primary oncall set to kevin at 12:52. Incident remains active and assigned to eng-oncall.
maria.s: jumping off now. Good job.
kevin: thanks — monitoring.
customer-success: closing CS loop for customers who accepted reroute. Will update after postmortem.
